about-time.evidence: Official publisher Mini Rules posted November 2012 by co-designer Joe Gill, successfully retrieved unchanged from its actual December 2012 public capture. This is the named Circa Circa historical-year guessing game, matching BGG 32337 and the local character/cardholder/TimeCard/token/centre mechanics, not unrelated clock-learning games. The archive requested through the older plural domain redirected to the actual singular abouttimeboardgame.com publisher site; its bounded historical index and linked pages supplied this primary reference, where the earlier plural-domain PDF-only search had not. The complete Mini Rules article was read, with complete selected 2010 primary game-elements page and signed 2010 token clarification as separately labelled supporting text. Together they provide character-at-Start setup, four initial TimeCards, initial one-token pot/no tokens distributed to players, youngest first, colour/category question, all-team 30-second written year guesses except Duels, answer reveal, nearest-year reward, exact-answer doubling, winner becoming next Reader and moving, first Time shout, Reader exclusion, five-token centre round, failed-centre return to Castle and most-tokens victory. The 2010 game-elements page supplies category/component use, Duel half-token transfer rounded down and Plague half-token pot effect. Accurate source type is publisher RULES REFERENCE HTML, not a recovered full printed rulebook, all original 2007/2008 pages or complete component deck. The Mini Rules explicitly refers to unavailable rulebook page 4 for full tied-round Rollover handling. All Highwayman/board-space details, every TimeCard and complete question-card/timeline components are not recovered or certified. The 2010 token clarification explicitly concerns the 2008 UK edition, while the 2012 Mini Rules is later publisher core guidance; texts remain dated and separate rather than silently declaring every edition identical. Its exchange sentence self-references tokens marked 10; this original textual ambiguity is retained verbatim, not used to invent a denomination-exchange procedure. Selected HTML excludes navigation/reviews, preserves source wording and normalizes only whitespace/line wrapping; all three unchanged originals and hashes remain available. Old playabouttime.com HTML was statically inspected but provided marketing/Flash-host text, not the missing full rules; no Flash was executed. One specific MAJOR Reader/TimeCard eligibility finding is recorded against the covered publisher Mini Rules; no complete summary audit, PASS or body repair.
